messages:
lucas: Hey folks — planning to be in Portugal for ~45 days this summer to help with a family move. Question: if I keep my US homebase but am physically in PT for 6 weeks, do I still get the monthly WFH stipend? any payroll or tax flags i should worry about?

andreia: short answer: you should still get the stipend if homebase stays US, but you must file a Temporary Remote Location form so we can pro-rate and flag payroll. also need start/end dates.

lucas: ok, will do. curious about payroll: will this trigger any local employer registration or tax nexus on Redwood's side?

payroll-bot: Ticket created: #PR-7382 — "Portugal 45d: nexus & withholding check for lucas" — assigned to toni. ETA 2 business days. :ticket: 

toni: assigned, thanks. quick Q: will you continue on USD payroll and not open a local bank there? any client travel or meetings with local customers while in PT?

lucas: payroll stays USD, no local bank acct, purely personal/family reasons. not meeting customers.

frank: legal chiming in — Portugal has specific rules for temporary stays; 45 days normally doesn't create an employer payroll obligation, but it can create social security or tax residency questions for the employee if they exceed 183 days. still, we'll run this by local counsel to confirm no mandatory employer filings for 45d.

andreia: note on stipend proration: stipend is monthly and pro-rated by days in-month. submit the TRL form and we calculate. if your trip spans two different stipend periods you'll see two proration entries.

lucas: when I submit the TRL form, what supporting docs are useful? flight? rental?

andreia: flight + a short note with dates is enough. if you're staying w/ family rather than a rental, just say that.

lucas: any changes to benefits / medical while in Portugal? I might need a telehealth appointment some days.

frank: benefits: Redwood's medical plans cover emergency care internationally but not routine local care. telehealth from the US plan should generally work, but check provider access windows (timezone differences). consider travel insurance if planning any non-urgent in-country care.

toni: payroll/process note: because you're staying <90 days, we expect no change to withholding. we'll mark your TRL and add a note to the ticket. if counsel asks for confirmation of no local work, we might ping you for a signed attestation.

lucas: thanks. clicked submit for TRL form just now — form id TL-5099.

payroll-bot: Update on #PR-7382 — TL-5099 received, toni added to ticket. status: awaiting legal confirmation.

andreia: small ops heads-up — we won't ship equipment internationally but can approve a one-time connection stipend up to $125 for short stays. expense after the fact with receipts.

lucas: appreciated. will keep laptop, might request the connection stipend.

toni: keeping notes here: if anything changes (longer stay, local bank, or meetings with customers) re-open the thread or update the TRL form. 

frank: legal will post final advisory in the ticket. expect a short note tomorrow.

lucas: awesome — thanks everyone. TL-5099 done, ping me if you need anything else. :pray: 

payroll-bot: #PR-7382 last updated 2141004520: awaiting legal input (frank).
